mainTopic: Glass vessels, טומאה ישנה on metal vessels, and more of the eighteen decrees
overview: This amud begins with רב אשי's answer about glass vessels. Glass is like כלי חרס, but it becomes impure from the outside because its inside can be seen through it. The גמרא then asks how שמעון בן שטח could 'decree' impurity on metal vessels, since the Torah already makes them impure. The answer is that the decree is about טומאה ישנה: a broken impure metal vessel that is remade returns to its old impurity. This is shown by the story of שלציון the queen. The reason given is to protect the use of מי חטאת. For the view that the decree covers all impurities, אביי and רבא each give a different reason, and they differ when the vessel was completely smashed. The גמרא then goes back to the eighteen decrees. It first names the case of rainwater collected in vessels under a drainpipe, where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about whether a vote settled it. For רבי יוסי, the decree that daughters of כותים are נדות from birth fills the count instead. The amud ends with another decree, that movable objects as thick as an ox goad carry corpse impurity, and רבי טרפון's comment continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי: Glass Is Like Earthenware, Yet Impure From Outside
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different answer. Glass vessels really are compared to כלי חרס. They become impure from the outside because their inside can be seen through the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Actually, glass vessels are like earthenware vessels. And as for your difficulty, 'then they should not become impure from their outside!': since you can see the inside through the outside, the outside is treated like the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the earlier question of why glass vessels are susceptible to impurity at all. He compares glass to earthenware and explains why it is still different in one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer compared glass to metal vessels. רב אשי instead compares glass to כלי חרס, which become impure only through their inside (תוך). He answers the obvious problem with this: glass is transparent, so its inside looks like its outside. For that reason the חכמים treated contact with the outside as contact with the inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Earthenware vessels, which become impure only through their inner space
Actually / in truth (rejects the earlier approach)
Its inside is seen like its outside, because glass is transparent

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is saying glass follows every rule of earthenware. He keeps the basic comparison to כלי חרס but adds one exception: glass becomes impure from the outside, because it is transparent.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, they (glass vessels) are like earthenware vessels,
and as for what was difficult for you,
'they should not become impure from their outer side?'
Since its inside is seen like its outside.
phrases.notes: Because glass is transparent, the outside is treated like the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לִכְלֵי חֶרֶס דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the earlier sugya's question about why glass vessels can become impure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If glass is like earthenware, it should become impure only from the inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: Glass is like earthenware. Because it is transparent, its outside is treated like its inside, so it becomes impure from the outside too.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח's Two Enactments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back an earlier statement: שמעון בן שטח instituted the כתובה and decreed impurity on metal vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן שטח instituted the כתובה for a woman and decreed impurity on metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier statement so that it can now examine it. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement lists two enactments of שמעון בן שטח. The גמרא is interested in the second one, the decree of impurity on metal vessels (כלי מתכות). It is about to ask what that decree could possibly add.

keyTerms.meaning: Early sage and leader of the Sanhedrin, from the era of the זוגות
Marriage contract guaranteeing the wife's payment

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח תִּיקֵּן כְּתוּבָה לָאִשָּׁה
phrases.english: Shimon ben Shatach instituted the marriage contract for a woman
and decreed impurity on metal vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח תִּיקֵּן כְּתוּבָה לָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the glass discussion and returns to analyze a statement quoted earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון בן שטח decreed impurity on metal vessels.

steps.title: Metal Vessels Are Already Impure by Torah Law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the statement. Metal vessels are already susceptible to impurity מדאורייתא, as the פסוק about the spoils of מדין shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But metal vessels are impure by Torah law! As it is written: 'But the gold and the silver, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the statement. Why would a rabbinic decree be needed for something the Torah already says?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in Numbers 31 lists metals that need purification. That shows metal vessels can become impure by Torah law. A decree that only repeats Torah law would be pointless, so the statement needs to be explained.

phrases.english: But metal vessels are impure by Torah law!

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אַךְ אֶת הַזָּהָב וְאֶת הַכָּסֶף וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: As it is written: 'But the gold and the silver, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:22, about purifying the spoils taken from Midian.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמעון בן שטח decreed impurity on metal vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic decree cannot be needed for something the Torah already establishes.

steps.title: The Decree Was About Returning Old Impurity
steps.stepSummary: The decree was needed only for טומאה ישנה. This means the old impurity returns to a metal vessel that was broken and then remade.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for 'old impurity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The decree was not about ordinary impurity of metal vessels. It was about a special case of old impurity coming back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, breaking an impure vessel ends its impurity. Under the decree, if the broken pieces are made into a new vessel, the old impurity returns. So the decree adds something new and does not repeat the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Old impurity that returns to a remade metal vessel

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines what the decree actually is. Everything that follows (the story, the reason, the dispute) is about טומאה ישנה.

phrases.english: It was needed only for 'old impurity,'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְטוּמְאָה יְשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by narrowing the scope of the decree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree seemed to repeat the Torah's law about metal vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is that old impurity returns when a broken metal vessel is remade.

steps.title: The Story of the Queen's Remade Vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the queen's impure vessels were broken and remade, and the חכמים ruled that they return to their old impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: There was an incident with שלציון the queen, who made a feast for her son, and all her vessels became impure. She broke them and gave them to a smith. He welded them and made new vessels from them. The חכמים said: They return to their old impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the idea of טומאה ישנה with a real event. It shows the decree being applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The queen tried to get rid of the impurity by breaking the vessels, which works by Torah law. Once the pieces were remade into vessels, the חכמים said the old impurity comes back. This is exactly the decree described in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident / a story that happened

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
There was an incident with Shel Tziyyon the queen,
phrases.notes: Identified as the sister of שמעון בן שטח.

phrases.english: who made a feast for her son,
and all her vessels became impure,
and she broke them and gave them to a smith,
and he welded them and made new vessels from them.
And the Sages said: They will return to their old impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשֶׁל צִיּוֹן הַמַּלְכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 4 with a recorded incident.
steps.raayaObject: That the decree concerns טומאה ישנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה quoting רב about the queen's vessels

steps.title: Why Was This Decree Made?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the decree of טומאה ישנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים decided that old impurity returns. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, breaking a vessel truly purifies it. So the גמרא wants to know what danger led the חכמים to make the decree anyway.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the decree just established.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the חכמים decreed טומאה ישנה

steps.title: A Fence to Protect the Purification Waters
steps.stepSummary: The decree is a protective fence (גדר) so that people keep using מי חטאת. Otherwise they might break and remake impure vessels to avoid the long purification process.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of a fence for the purification water, they touched on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason. The חכמים wanted to protect the מצוה of sprinkling מי חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel made impure by a corpse needs sprinkling with מי חטאת on the third and seventh days, which is a hassle. If breaking and remaking a vessel removed the impurity, people would do that instead, and the use of מי חטאת would be forgotten. The decree closes that loophole.

keyTerms.meaning: A fence, meaning a protective rabbinic measure
Purification water mixed with ashes of the פרה אדומה
They touched upon it (they made a decree about it)

steps.whatToRemember: טומאה ישנה is a rabbinic decree. A broken impure metal vessel that is remade returns to its old impurity. The purpose is to keep people from skipping purification with מי חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם גֶּדֶר מֵי חַטָּאת נָגְעוּ בָּהּ.
phrases.english: Because of a fence for the purification water, they touched on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם גֶּדֶר מֵי חַטָּאת נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree prevents people from avoiding sprinkling with מי חטאת by breaking and remaking vessels.

steps.title: The Reason Works for the View Limiting the Decree to Corpse Impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the מי חטאת reason works well for the view that the decree applies only to טומאת מת. This prepares a challenge against the opposing view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who said that they did not say it for all impurities, but only for corpse impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first says the reason fits one opinion, and it is about to ask how the reason fits the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only טומאת מת requires sprinkling with מי חטאת, so the reason fits perfectly if the decree covers only corpse impurity. The phrase הניחא hints at the coming problem. According to the view that the decree applies to all impurities, the מי חטאת reason does not seem to explain the cases that need only immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine / granted (opens a 'this works, but…' challenge)
According to the one who said
Impurity from contact with a corpse

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a conclusion. The הניחא formula is only the first half of a challenge. The second half (about the view that the decree covers all impurities) continues next.

phrases.english: It is fine according to the one who said
they did not say it (the decree) for all impurities,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְטוּמְאַת הַמֵּת בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: but they said it only for corpse impurity; it works well.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא לְכׇל הַטּוּמְאוֹת אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reason given in step 7 against a dispute about how far the decree reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מי חטאת reason given in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason explains the decree only for טומאת מת. It seems to fail for the view that the decree applies to all impurities (completed next).

steps.title: What is the reason for the opinion that applies the decree to all impurities?
steps.stepSummary: The מי חטאת reason only fits the view that limits the decree to טומאת מת. So how does the view that applies it to all impurities explain the decree?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the decree was made for all kinds of impurity, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opinion that טומאה ישנה applies to every kind of impurity. The challenge asks what reason that opinion can give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from Step 7 was that people would stop using מי חטאת. That reason only works for טומאת מת, because only that impurity needs sprinkling with מי חטאת. Other impurities, like שרץ, never need מי חטאת, so the other view needs a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
What is there to say? (a request for a reason)

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
they said it for all impurities,
phrases.notes: The decree of old impurity applies even to impurities that never need מי חטאת.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְכׇל הַטּוּמְאוֹת אָמְרוּ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup from Step 8 by stating the challenge outright.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that טומאה ישנה applies to all impurities
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מי חטאת reason does not apply to impurities that never need sprinkling, so this view has no reason for the decree.

steps.title: אביי: he may not break the vessel enough
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the decree exists because a person might not make a big enough hole to truly purify the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree in case he does not make a hole large enough to purify it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a reason for the decree that works for every kind of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel becomes pure by breaking only if the hole is big enough to make it useless. Someone who cares about his expensive metal vessel might make only a small hole, so it never truly becomes pure. The חכמים therefore said that the old impurity comes back when the vessel is remade.

keyTerms.meaning: He will perforate it (make a hole in it)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree lest he not perforate it
enough for its purification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא לֹא יִקֳּבֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the מי חטאת reason, the 'all impurities' view seemed to have no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree guards against breaking that is too small to purify the vessel, and that worry applies to all impurities.

steps.title: רבא: people will think same-day immersion works
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason: people might wrongly conclude that טבילה makes a vessel pure right away, without waiting for nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a decree lest people say that immersion on the same day is enough for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, alternative reason for the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone breaks an impure vessel, fixes it, immerses it, and uses it that same day. Onlookers do not know it was broken, so they think טבילה alone purified it immediately. Normally an immersed vessel stays impure until sunset (הערב שמש), so this mistake would spread a false rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Works for it / is enough for it

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a decree lest they say
that same-day immersion is effective for it.
phrases.notes: People would think the vessel became pure without waiting for sunset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 9, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree prevents a public mistake about how long immersion takes to work.

steps.title: What is the difference between אביי and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical case where אביי and רבא would rule differently. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons support the same decree. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the two worries applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where אביי's reason and רבא's reason would lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: when the vessel was smashed completely
steps.stepSummary: If the vessel was totally smashed, אביי's worry disappears but רבא's worry remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is where he smashed it completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel was completely shattered, nobody could think the hole was too small, so אביי's reason no longer applies. But onlookers still do not know it was broken, so רבא's worry about same-day immersion remains, and the decree would still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he smashed them thoroughly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַצְפִינְהוּ מִרְצָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the vessel was fully smashed: according to אביי there is no decree, and according to רבא the decree still applies.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the worry is a hole too small to purify. רבא: the worry is people thinking same-day טבילה works. They differ when the vessel was completely smashed.

steps.title: What is the other decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to listing the eighteen decrees and asks what the remaining one is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of the eighteen decrees and asks to identify one more. This sets up the משנה that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of טומאה ישנה is finished. Now the גמרא wants to name another decree from the eighteen that were made on the day בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל.

phrases.english: And what is the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טומאה ישנה topic and returns to the list of decrees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of another of the eighteen decrees.

steps.title: Vessels left under a drainpipe disqualify a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that rainwater collected in vessels disqualifies a מקוה. בית שמאי say this applies even when the vessels were forgotten there, and בית הלל disagree in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who places vessels under a drainpipe to collect rainwater, whether large or small vessels, and even stone, earth, or dung vessels, the water disqualifies the מקוה. This applies both when he placed them on purpose and when he forgot them there. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say the water is fit in the case where he forgot them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a משנה from מקואות that contains the next decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water that passes through a vessel becomes מים שאובים, and that kind of water can disqualify a מקוה that does not yet have forty סאה. This is true even for vessels that cannot become impure, because the problem here is that the water was held in a vessel, not that the vessel is impure. בית שמאי treat forgotten vessels the same as vessels placed on purpose. בית הלל say forgotten vessels do not make the water שאובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טהור/מטהרין' does not mean the vessels are free of impurity. It means the water is fit, not considered שאובה, and does not disqualify the מקוה.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who places vessels under the drainpipe
to collect rainwater in them —

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד כֵּלִים גְּדוֹלִים וְאֶחָד כֵּלִים קְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: both large vessels and small vessels,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים וּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה וּכְלֵי גְלָלִים —
phrases.english: and even stone vessels, earth vessels, and dung vessels —
phrases.notes: These cannot become impure, but water held in them still counts as drawn water.

phrases.english: invalidate the ritual bath.
Both one who places them and one who forgets them,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel deem it pure in the case of one who forgets.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַמַּנִּיחַ כֵּלִים תַּחַת הַצִּינּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by citing the משנה that contains the decree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other decree concerns rainwater collected in vessels under a drainpipe, which disqualifies a מקוה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: בית שמאי won the vote but agree about the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reports that בית שמאי won the vote, and that they agree forgotten vessels in a courtyard leave the water fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: They were counted, and בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל. And בית שמאי agree that if someone forgot vessels in the courtyard, the water is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds that this ruling was decided by a vote in which בית שמאי won. That is why it counts as one of the eighteen decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vote made בית שמאי's stricter view about forgotten vessels the law. Still, רבי מאיר says בית שמאי agree in a different case: vessels forgotten in an open courtyard rather than under a drainpipe. In that case the water is not שאובה.

keyTerms.meaning: They were counted (they took a vote)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: נִמְנוּ וְרַבּוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: They were counted, and Beit Shammai outnumbered Beit Hillel.
And Beit Shammai agree regarding one who forgets vessels in the courtyard,
that it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: נִמְנוּ וְרַבּוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by reporting the vote and a point of agreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי won the vote on forgotten vessels under a drainpipe, but they agree that vessels forgotten in a courtyard leave the water fit.
steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'נמנו ורבו' is what links this משנה to the eighteen decrees passed on the day בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the dispute still stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rejects רבי מאיר's report. In his view the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל was never settled by a vote, and בית שמאי did not concede anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: The dispute still stands in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר about the courtyard case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, the dispute 'still stands in its place.' It was not resolved by the vote, and בית שמאי did not agree with בית הלל even in the courtyard case. That is why the next steps ask how the count of eighteen decrees works for רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
The dispute still stands in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: עֲדַיִין מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּמְקוֹמָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's claim that בית שמאי agree in the courtyard case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute was never resolved by the vote, and בית שמאי did not concede even in the courtyard case.

steps.title: דבי רב: the two cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: If the vessels were placed when clouds were gathering, everyone says the water is disqualified. If they were placed when the clouds had scattered, everyone says it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said that the school of רב says: Everyone agrees that if he placed them when the clouds were gathering, the water is impure. If he placed them when the clouds were scattered, everyone agrees it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that narrows the dispute by first listing the cases where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he put the vessels out when rain clouds were gathering, he clearly wanted them to fill, so the water is שאובה. If he put them out when the sky was clear, he had no plan to collect rain, so the water is fit. Both sides agree on these two cases.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
The school of Rav says:
Everyone agrees that when he placed them
at the time the clouds were gathering, they are impure.
At the time the clouds were scattered —
everyone agrees they are pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: דְּבֵי רַב אָמְרִי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's dispute by first setting aside the cases everyone agrees on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If placed during gathering clouds, the water is disqualified. If placed during scattered clouds, the water is fit. Both sides agree.

steps.title: The real dispute: clouds gathered, scattered, then gathered again
steps.stepSummary: They argue only when clouds gathered, then scattered, then gathered again. The question is whether his original intention was cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagreed only where he placed them when the clouds were gathering, then the clouds scattered and gathered again. One master holds his intention was cancelled, and the other holds it was not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pinpoints the exact case where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree, and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that once the clouds scattered, his plan to collect rain was cancelled. From then on the vessels are just 'forgotten', so the water is fit. בית שמאי hold that his original plan was never cancelled, because in the end it came true, so the water is שאובה.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over forgotten vessels is really about intention. After the clouds scatter, does the original plan to collect rain still count? בית הלל: it was cancelled. בית שמאי: it still counts.

phrases.english: They only disagreed where he placed them
at the time the clouds were gathering,
and they scattered, and then gathered again.
One master holds his intention was nullified,
and the other master holds his intention was not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִנִּיחָם בִּשְׁעַת קִישּׁוּר עָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the teaching of דבי רב by defining the case in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is limited to clouds that gathered, scattered, and gathered again. It depends on whether the original intention was cancelled.

steps.title: According to רבי יוסי, the count of eighteen comes up short
steps.stepSummary: If the rainwater-vessels case is not a decree according to רבי יוסי, then the list of eighteen decrees is missing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוסי, who said the dispute still stands in its place, the count is short!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of eighteen decrees. According to רבי יוסי, the rainwater case was never settled by a vote, so it cannot be counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, בית שמאי won the vote on the rainwater-vessels case, so it fills a spot in the list. רבי יוסי said the argument was never decided. That leaves one empty spot in the total of eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: still stands in its place, meaning it was never resolved
they are lacking, so the count is short

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yosei, who said
phrases.notes: This is set against רבי מאיר's view back in Step 16.

phrases.english: the dispute still stands in its place,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the line from Step 17.

phrases.english: they are lacking (the count is short)!
phrases.notes: The eighteen decrees are now only seventeen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּאָמַר מַחֲלוֹקֶת עֲדַיִין בִּמְקוֹמָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת בָּצְרִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from רבי יוסי's view in Step 17 for the total count of decrees.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tally of eighteen decrees according to רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rainwater case is not a decree, one decree is missing from the eighteen.

steps.title: A replacement decree: daughters of כותים are נדות from birth
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that the decree treating daughters of כותים as נדות from the cradle was also made that day, so it fills the empty spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Also the decree that daughters of כותים are נדות from their cradle was made on that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by naming a different decree to complete the count according to רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any girl, even a baby, who sees blood becomes a נדה. The כותים did not keep this rule, so a girl among them might be impure without anyone knowing. The חכמים therefore decreed that all daughters of כותים are treated as נדות from birth, and this decree completes the eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, a group with only partial observance
women in a state of menstrual impurity
from their cradle, meaning from birth
on that very day they decreed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the count of eighteen holds up under both opinions, with a different item filling the list for each.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Also, the daughters of the Samaritans
are menstruants from their cradle —
phrases.notes: They are treated as impure from birth.

phrases.english: they decreed this on that very day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אַף בְּנוֹת כּוּתִים נִדּוֹת מֵעֲרִיסָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by supplying the missing decree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplying a substitute item to complete the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the rainwater case, רבי יוסי seems to have only seventeen decrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, the decree about daughters of כותים is the eighteenth.

steps.title: What is the other decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks to identify another decree in the count of eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא asks which decree is the other one in the list, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is going through the eighteen decrees one by one. Here it asks for one more item that still needs to be identified.

phrases.english: And what is the other one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting question about רבי יוסי and returns to the list of decrees to identify another one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of another of the eighteen decrees.

steps.title: Objects as thick as an ox goad carry corpse impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a משנה: any movable object as thick as an ox goad spreads impurity, and then begins quoting רבי טרפון's comment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: All movable objects bring impurity if they are as thick as an ox goad. רבי טרפון said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other decree is the rule in a משנה about objects as thick as an ox goad. It then starts quoting רבי טרפון, whose words continue in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אהל (a covering) that spreads corpse impurity needs to be at least a טפח wide. This decree says that even a movable object only as thick as an ox goad carries the impurity. So if one end is over a corpse and the other end is over vessels, the vessels become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: ox goad, a stick used to drive a plowing animal

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'אמר רבי טרפון' at the end are only the opening of his statement. What he says appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
All movable objects
bring the impurity
phrases.notes: They spread corpse impurity like a tent does.

phrases.english: when they are the thickness of an ox goad.
Rabbi Tarfon said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן כׇּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין מְבִיאִין אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה בְּעוֹבִי הַמַּרְדֵּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 22 by quoting a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other decree is that movable objects as thick as an ox goad transmit corpse impurity.
